pr_body:
This implements CFB one shots.

Some implementation notes:

1. As discovered in #55477, CFB128 and CFB64 do not work with persisted CNG keys, they always work in CFB8 mode today. Rather than replicating this wrong behavior, the `AesCng` and `TripleDESCng` one shots will throw if the key is persisted and the feedback size is other than 8. This limitation can be removed, if it is possible, when the linked issue is solved.
2. This does not change the behavior of the `ICryptoTransform` CFB implementation. The CNG CFB128 /CFB64 persisted-key remain as-is (using CFB8). 
2. RC2 does not support CFB at all, so the implementation throws.

Closes #2406

review_comments: This is our detection mechanism to determine if `BasicSymmetricCipherNCrypt` or `BasicSymmetricCipherBCrypt` is going to be used. The former does not correctly handle feedback sizes other than CFB8.

This "worked" but was technically wrong - the padding amount is always based on the feedback size. However, since the only other feedback size supported other than CFB8 was block-size CFB, (CFB64 for 3DES and CFB128 for AES) it all worked anyway. This just does it "right" without changing the behavior.
This variable name was bad - `FeedbackSize` was in bits.

In the final analysis I think this is OK, but here are thoughts I had in the meantime.

* The caller specifying the feedback size seems like they probably know that the only two valid options are 8 and alg.BlockSize, so an ArgumentException seems more appropriate.
* The case of persisted keys only doing CFB8 is different, they wouldn't really know they hit a provider limitation, so that's not an ArgumentException.
* Yeah, CreateEncryptor/CreateDecryptor throws CryptographicException for this, but that's because they didn't take arguments, they took property state.
* Wait, they don't throw there, because the property validates.  So back to ArgumentException.
* Double wait, those validating properties throw CryptographicException.
* I think I might still prefer ArgumentException.  Except we'd have to figure out the model for CFB{block}+persisted CNG.
* Matching is good, though.
* Eh, it's fine how it is.
Yeah I used the property setter as inspiration.

The if this is associated with describes that DES3+CFB64 doesn't work on Windows 7, but there's only one test case in the block and 11 that were added unconditionally.

I think this close curly is supposed to move down a fair bit :)
I'm not sure... I understand here. The `if` and its closing brace appear to be in the right place to me... that curly brace you left a comment on is for the `new object[]` construction, not the `if`.

So it is.  And everything's properly indented, so it's not that.

Apparently something just mis-fired in my brain.

Small deviation from the approved API: `feedbackSizeBits` was changed to `feedbackSizeInBits`. This is to match the same decision that was done in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/45003#discussion_r527795851.
